sections.content: You know the polite *condicional* from A2 Unit 26 (*¿Podría cambiar mi habitación?*), the polite *imperfecto* from B2 Unit 2 (*Quería pedirle un favor*), *me parece que* from B1 Unit 7 and hedging from B2 Unit 21. Together they make a request or an opinion gentle. With *usted* they are the normal way to ask a stranger for something.

This lesson adds two more tools. *¿Le importaría + infinitive?* means "would you mind…?" and is very polite. *Yo diría que…* ("I would say that…") gives an opinion without pushing it. To disagree gently, first accept the other view, then give yours with *me parece que*.

sections.title: From blunt to gentle
rows: Quiero hablar con el director. → Quería hablar con el director.
I want to speak to the director. → I was wondering if I could speak to the director.
Abra la ventana. → ¿Podría abrir la ventana?
Open the window. → Could you open the window?
Cierre la puerta. → ¿Le importaría cerrar la puerta?
Close the door. → Would you mind closing the door?
Está equivocado. → Yo diría que está equivocado.
You are wrong. → I would say you are mistaken.
No es verdad. → Entiendo, pero me parece que no es verdad.
That's not true. → I see, but it seems to me that it isn't true.

sections.content: One softener is enough: *Quería pedirle un favor* is polite; *Quería preguntarle si no le importaría…* is heavy. After *¿Le importaría…?* the verb is an infinitive: *¿Le importaría esperar?*
